imageRegistry.caption: Transvaginal color Doppler US shows a hemorrhagic corpus luteal cyst in a pregnant woman with pelvic pain. It is filled with low-level echoes and has peripheral increased vascularity, "ring of fire" . This can be confused with an ectopic pregnancy, but most ectopics are located in the fallopian tube and can be separated from the ovary by exerting gentle pressure with the probe.

imageRegistry.caption: Axial T1WI FS MR should always be performed, as it increases lesion conspicuity and rules out a fat-containing lesion. Hemorrhagic cysts are quite variable in signal intensity, reflecting both the age and concentration of blood products.

imageRegistry.caption: Transvaginal US in the same patient shows low-level echoes with a slight reticular pattern typical of a hemorrhagic cyst . Note the posterior acoustic enhancement . In the reproductive age group, hemorrhagic cysts with a classic appearance do not require follow-up unless > 5 cm.

imageRegistry.caption: Axial T1WI MR shows a predominately hypointense left ovarian cyst with a vague, hyperintense fluid-fluid level posteriorly . While the classic teaching is that hemorrhagic cysts are hyperintense on T1WI, they are actually quite variable, with many being hypointense, the result of a small amount of hemorrhage in a relatively larger amount of fluid within the cyst.

The margins of the ovary are obscured, and there is variable echogenicity, ill-defined material within the pelvis , representing clotted and unclotted blood.
